text: Their musical instruments include the gagong, kolintang, and durugan. The Manobo (Manuvu, Minuvu) inhabit core areas from Sarangani island and the provinces of Agusan del Sur, Davao provinces, Bukidnon, and North and South Cotabato.

text: Mar 27, 2025 · The Manobo are also known for their music, dance, and rituals, which are deeply spiritual in nature. Gongs, bamboo flutes, and drums accompany dances that reenact animal movements, agricultural cycles, and courtship.

text: Dibabawon Manobo is a stable indigenous language of the Philippines. It belongs to the Austronesian language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
